notes: Smallest tool-less round-trip pinning the terminal-text end signal for Muse: a run's own terminal:"completed" record maps to turn_done (parser.go parseRunTerminal), IsAgentDone()=true with no open tool call, no PendingWaitingCue from the declarative reply, classifier rule 2b fires working→ready. CORRECTED per #1960 record pass (session 01a09dc6-05b5-7711-843f-3a725938ff43, recording 2026-09-14-04-36-35): (1) session-birth shape is now live-confirmed as a direct single birth — the real session reaches ready via 'new session created' before any proc-<PID> presession appears (presession_created lands ~400-600ms later and is immediately superseded); session_birth stays structurally unpinned since the birth shape isn't guaranteed cross-run, but is now known to resolve to the real session in practice. (2) turn_start was previously left unpinned on the theory that 'the FIRST session to go working anywhere must be the real session — a pre-session never processes a turn'. That theory missed a real actor: muse spawns goal-reminder/verify-reminder SUBAGENTS for every prompt (format-spec §9), and those subagent sessions go straight to working (skipping ready) BEFORE the parent session's own turn starts. The unpinned matcher therefore silently bound turn_start (and everything chained off it via same_session_as) to a subagent's own turn, not the parent's — a genuine vacuous-pass risk this same recording exposed via its teardown phase failing implausibly. Fixed by pinning turn_start to same_session_as:session_birth (subagents never pass through a ready birth, so they can never satisfy this filter). (3) pid_bind's relative_to was 'turn_start', but the real session's PID binds immediately after session_birth (within ~200ms), well before its own turn_start — anchoring pid_bind after the (now correctly-pinned, much later) turn_start would never find a match, so pid_bind now anchors to session_birth instead, same_session_as:session_birth. (4) The teardown phase (process_exited on the real/parent session) is REMOVED from this cell: this recipe never issues exit_clean (tmux kill only), and under that path process_exited is only reliably attributable to the parent session when the parent's PID gets a LATE re-discovery event after any subagents' own pid_discovered calls (confirmed in the sibling session-start and basic-turn recordings, both of which show a second, later pid_discovered for the real session). This recording's parent session got only its early pid_discovery, so the daemon's shared-PID exit watcher (processlifecycle: pidMonitor.watched map[int]string in monitor_darwin.go/monitor_linux.go Watch(), last-write-wins per PID) attributed the eventual process_exited to whichever subagent session (0f6d6927-4e36-4b20-8a3e-3763f353176b) most recently re-registered that PID instead — the parent session received NO process_exited event at all. This is a genuine, reproducible daemon race (not specific to this recipe's timing) that basic-turn's exit_clean-driven teardown phase already covers and reliably passes against, so this cell drops the redundant, racy assertion rather than gate its own (unrelated) purpose on a bug that's tracked separately. Overlaps intentionally with basic-turn — this cell pins the end-signal mechanism specifically, not teardown/process-exit attribution.

text: A session (real, or a transient proc-<PID> pre-session) appears in ready within 2s of launch
User prompt drives ready → working on the SAME session that was born ready (subagents skip ready and start at working directly, so this filter excludes them; a pre-session never goes working)
terminal:"completed" on the run closes the turn → turn_done → working → ready; state never entered waiting
PID bound to the real session via its .session.lock shortly after birth (well before the turn itself starts)
